newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Beijing North Star to tap New World skills.
newsitem.headline: Beijing North Star to tap New World skills.

text.p: The Beijing government-backed Beijing North Star Co Ltd said on Monday it will draw on the expertise of the New World group, a Hong Kong developer, to improve efficiency and profitability.

"After the share listing, we will establish a strategic relationship with the New World Group, which has a 9.6 percent stake in our company," Beijing North Star chairman Sha Wanquen told a news conference.
Beijing North Star said earlier it was issuing 614.8 million H-shares at HK$2.40, of which 171.10 million were being placed with Rich Funds Ltd, a subsidiary of New World China.

"Furthermore, by drawing on the international expertise of the strategic partner, the New World Group, Beijing North Star is well positioned to build on its solid foundations, to enhance profitability and to continue its growth," the chairman said.
But he did not disclose any plans for the two to cooperate.
Beijing North Star is principally engaged in property investment and development in Beijing.
It had also completed a placement of 351.48 million H-shares with international investors, which was 40 times subscribed, said an executive of HSBC Investment Bank Asia, which managed the issue.
Because of the warm response to the placement, it had lifted its proposed H-share issue price range to between HK$2.16 and HK$2.40 from HK$1.99 to HK$2.32 previously, he said.
He said the HK$2.40 issue price represented an 18.9 percent discount to adjusted net tangible asset value of 3.17 yuan a share.
Sha said Beijing North Star's investment portfolio was in the Asian Games Village nine km from the city's centre.
It had a convention centre, a four-star hotel, 12 commercial/residentialblocks and an office tower, he said.

In its listing document, the company said the investment properties were valued at 2.48 billion yuan as at February 28, and accounted for about 42.20 percent of its 5.86 billion yuan property portfolio,the chairman.
Sha also said the company would focus on residential properties to exploit rising housing demand in Beijing and to comply with government development policies.
"More than half of our properties under development are for residential purposes," he added.
It had won official approval to develop Bei Yuan Residential Estates in Wa Li, 11 km north of Beijing city centre, he said.
The company said in the listing document that on completion, Bei Yuan Residential Estate would have gross floor area of over 1.30 million square metres. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6369
